title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
authors: YanKai Chen, Zhi Wan, ZiHao Li, Tao Jing
abstract: Using large language models to interpret experimental evidence, design discriminating experiments and formulate well-supported mechanistic explanations remains a central challenge in materials research. Here we establish PSM-Bench, an 800-question benchmark developed by perovskite researchers to evaluate scientific reasoning in perovskite photovoltaics. We also introduce OpenPerov, an expert-informed language-model framework that learns from expert-calibrated evidence records reconstructed from 4,035 training articles; these records link experimental strategies, controls and observations to mechanistic interpretations. Structured-evidence adaptation outperformed conventional question-answer training, and OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems. OpenPerov Pro raised Scientific Mastery further, from 87.6 to 89.1, by revising selected passages with retrieved evidence. On questions derived from subsequent studies, both models also outscored expert-authored answers. In an experimental test of self-assembled monolayer design, OpenPerov selected a K analogue that outperformed the Na analogue preferred by experts. Devices incorporating the selected contact reached a power conversion efficiency of 27.05% and retained 96.74% of their initial efficiency after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 $^\circ$C. These results show that reconstructed scientific reasoning provides an effective basis for building domain models that interpret experiments and inform materials design.

infographic.key_insight: Training on structured experimental evidence enabled OpenPerov to reason about perovskite solar cells and select a contact material that outperformed the expert-preferred alternative.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Evidence-grounded AI could guide contact-material selection and experimental design to improve solar-cell efficiency and thermal stability.
method: Reconstructed expert-calibrated evidence records from 4,035 articles, linking strategies, controls and observations to mechanisms.
Adapted OpenPerov using structured evidence; added retrieval-based passage revision in OpenPerov Pro.
Evaluated scientific reasoning and experimentally tested K- versus Na-analogue self-assembled monolayer contacts.
infographic.evidence_signal: On the 800-question PSM-Bench, OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems; devices using the selected contact reached 27.05% efficiency and retained 96.74% after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 °C.
infographic.watch_item: The reported contact-design test does not establish broad materials generalization, scalable manufacturing or stability under illuminated operating conditions.
infographic.paper_title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization

title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
authors: Zixu Huang, Julisa Juarez, Akash Dasgupta, David S. Ginger
abstract: Buried interfaces play a critical role in the operational stability of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet remain challenging to probe non-destructively. Here, we demonstrate a multiwavelength photoluminescence-based approach exploiting the wavelength-dependent absorption of perovskites, enabling fast, and non-destructive probing of depth-sensitive degradation behavior of perovskite devices under operational conditions. Using ultraviolet (UV) light-soaking with different indium tin oxide (ITO) modifiers as a test case, we employ wide-field photoluminescence (PL) imaging, time-resolved photoluminescence (trPL) and ideality factor measurements with different wavelength excitation to characterize degradation behavior of both perovskite thin films and photovoltaic devices under UV soaking. Using only nondestructive characterization, we show that UV-induced degradation in p-i-n perovskite solar cells occurs preferentially at the HTL interface, adversely affecting device stability, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests. Our results also show that modifying the buried interface with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane reduces UV-induced damage at the buried interface, thus improving the UV stability of both perovskite films and devices. This work establishes a fast, non-destructive strategy to screen depth-dependent degradation in perovskite devices, offering insights for interface design and stability optimization.

infographic.key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage in perovskite solar cells, with degradation concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive degradation screening can guide interface design, including 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification to improve UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths with photoluminescence excitation.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL and ideality-factor measurements during UV-soaking studies.
Compare perovskite films and p-i-n devices with different ITO interface modifiers.
infographic.evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements identified preferential buried-interface degradation consistent with ex-situ destructive tests and showed reduced UV damage with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports UV-soaking results without quantitative stability gains or evidence of generalization to other operational stressors.
infographic.paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors

title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yezeyuan Zheng, Ziyang Hu, Maojun Sun. Ruijian Han, Jian Huang, Guanhua Chen, Jie Liu
abstract: Experimental optimization of perovskite solar cells is constrained by combinatorial diversity in absorber compositions, device layers, and processing, which makes virtual screening attractive for prioritizing recipes before fabrication. We develop a surrogate-guided reinforcement-learning framework that casts recipe generation as virtual screening, enriching candidate shortlists near high-performing experimental neighbors. A frozen Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) guides recipe generation, while a reference pool of 890 measured devices enables neighborhood-based assessment. Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices shows top-ten selection raises mean power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 19.68\% to 23.74\%. Three learned policies are compared with six baselines under 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run. In top-100 shortlists, Proximal policy optimization (PPO) and recurrent PPO (RPPO) achieve neighborhood-supported hit rates of 23\% and 24\% (7.9- and 8.3-fold Pure Random's 2.9\%), versus 10\% (3.4-fold) for the baselines with the highest supported hit rate (L-SHADE and Ax BO, tied) at $K = 100$. Gains coexist with weak-support fractions. Of 9,000 recipes, 65.4\% match a composition family at similarity 0.80, falling to 11.7\% at 0.90. Results support enrichment-oriented prioritization but not experimental performance, seed robustness, or matched-budget advantage.

infographic.key_insight: Surrogate-guided reinforcement learning enriches perovskite recipe shortlists with candidates near high-performing measured devices, without establishing experimental performance.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could help prioritize solar-cell recipes for fabrication across large composition, device-layer, and processing design spaces.
method: Use a frozen Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) to guide recipe generation.
Compare three learned policies with six baselines using 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run.

title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
authors: Jiaxin Wu, Hongzhuo Wu, Zuhong Zhang, Xiaoyu Guan, Jinbo Zhao, Yuting Guo
abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl- induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal cycling.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Engineering adhesion at transparent-conductive-oxide/SAM interfaces offers a route to more durable, high-efficiency perovskite photovoltaics.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide to guide ordered self-assembled monolayer (SAM) formation.
Increase surface hydroxyl species to enable multipoint anchoring dominated by metal–oxygen coordination.
Use chloride-induced hydrogen bonding to cooperatively reinforce interfacial anchoring.
infographic.evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles from −40 to 85 °C under ISOS-T-3.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether these gains persist in large-area modules or under combined outdoor stressors.
infographic.paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells

title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Ying Tang, Zuhong Zhang, Hongzhuo Wu, Zhihao Li, Zhenhuang Su, Yonggang Yang
abstract: Tin-based perovskites are promising candidates for lead-free photovoltaics but suffer from labile Sn$^{2+}$ coordination, rapid crystallization, and severe interfacial defects. Here, we develop a dynamic molecular transformation using 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) to regulate crystallization and interface chemistry simultaneously. During nucleation and growth, the carbonyl group coordinates with Sn$^{2+}$ to stabilize precursor complexes, moderate supersaturation, and enable controlled crystal growth. Upon annealing, PX undergoes in situ molecular transformation, suggested to form amidinium-functionalized species that preferentially occupy surface A-site vacancies, forming a passivation layer and suppressing nonradiative recombination. This coupled bulk-to-interface evolution yields compact, highly crystalline films with improved optoelectronic quality. Devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.18% and retain 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 h of continuous illumination. This work demonstrates a dynamic molecular engineering approach integrating crystallization control and interface passivation, providing a pathway toward efficient and stable lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Dynamic transformation of 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) couples crystallization control with interface passivation in lead-free tin-based perovskite solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: A single additive offers a route to improved film quality, reduced interfacial recombination, and more efficient, stable tin-based photovoltaics.
method: Coordinate PX carbonyl groups with Sn²⁺ to stabilize precursor complexes and control crystal growth.
Anneal films to induce PX transformation into proposed amidinium-functionalized species.
Passivate surface A-site vacancies to suppress nonradiative recombination.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports 15.18% power conversion efficiency and retention of 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 hours of continuous illumination.
infographic.watch_item: The transformed species are proposed rather than definitively identified; their chemistry and processing reproducibility require further validation.
infographic.paper_title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells

title: How to Effectively Manage the Energy in Residential Systems: Development and Comparison of Methods
authors: Julian Ruddick
abstract: The transition from fossil fuels presents significant challenges in energy management. To ensure a sustainable energy future, it is crucial to reduce energy consumption when possible and to synchronize electricity consumption and storage with the production from sources with low greenhouse gas emissions. This thesis explores a variety of energy management methods used to manage batteries, heat pumps, and other energy-related systems. The thesis presents three simulation cases alongside one real-world experiment to compare energy management done through simple rules, optimization, and machine learning methods. Furthermore, this thesis introduces TreeC, a novel machine learning-based method that learns understandable yet efficient energy management strategies, applicable to many cases. The three key contributions of this thesis can be summarized as follows: 1) The developed TreeC method demonstrates competitive performance compared to a variety of energy management approaches, such as model predictive control and reinforcement learning, across a diverse set of energy management problems. The understandability of TreeC's energy management strategies greatly improves the transparency and trustworthiness of machine learning-based energy management. 2) The real-world experiment highlights the need to validate energy management methods on actual hardware and not solely on simulations. Both TreeC and model predictive control performed worse than in simulations, due to, respectively, insufficiently representative training data and the real-time input data not being reliable enough. 3) Energy management algorithms reduce costs in electrified Belgian dwellings, particularly in poorly insulated dwellings, electric vehicle chargers, and photovoltaic installations. However, on average, these cost savings do not yet outweigh the current costs and effort required to implement such algorithms.

infographic.key_insight: TreeC learns understandable residential energy-management strategies with performance competitive with model predictive control and reinforcement learning.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Coordinating batteries, heat pumps, EV charging, and photovoltaic systems can lower household energy costs, but implementation costs may outweigh savings.
method: Compare rule-based, optimization, and machine-learning energy management.
Develop TreeC to learn understandable control strategies.
Evaluate methods through simulations and a real-world experiment.
infographic.evidence_signal: Three simulation cases and one real-world experiment showed competitive TreeC performance, but both TreeC and model predictive control performed worse on hardware than in simulation.
infographic.watch_item: Deployment requires representative training data and reliable real-time inputs; average savings do not yet offset current implementation costs and effort.
infographic.paper_title: How to Effectively Manage the Energy in Residential Systems: Development and Comparison of Methods

title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
authors: Lijun Chen, Sitong Zhao, Gaukhar Nigmetova, David Garcia Romero, Matteo Pitaro, Sofia Lerda
abstract: Interfacial nonradiative recombination limits tin-lead perovskite photovoltaics. Here we show that neutral ethylenediamine chelates undercoordinated metals at tin-rich surfaces, weakens metal-iodide bonds, and removes excess tin, reconstructing the surface towards a stoichiometric tin-to-lead ratio. In contrast, protonated ethylenediammonium iodide initially passivates undercoordinated metal sites before undergoing defect-assisted deprotonation. Atomistic simulations reveal that subsurface iodide vacancies promote iodide migration and lower the energetic cost of deprotonation. Ethylenediamine-induced reconstruction produces stronger n-type surface character, facilitates electron extraction into C60, and suppresses interfacial nonradiative recombination, enabling methylammonium-free solar cells with a power conversion efficiency of 25.86%. Together, these distinct surface reaction pathways and the defect-assisted evolution of the passivating species underscore the importance of understanding perovskite surface chemistry for the rational design of molecular passivation strategies.

infographic.key_insight: Ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces by removing excess tin, improving electron extraction and suppressing interfacial nonradiative recombination.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Controlling molecular passivation chemistry offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free tin–lead perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine with protonated ethylenediammonium iodide surface treatments.
Use atomistic simulations to probe iodide migration and defect-assisted deprotonation.
Connect surface reconstruction to n-type character and electron extraction into C60.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term operational stability or scalability of the surface treatment.
infographic.paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells

title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells
authors: Zhaoheng Ling, Linqu Luo, Chrysa Aivalioti, Temur Maksudov, Mengxi Zhang, Theodoulos Kalogerakis
abstract: Tellurium dioxide (TeO$_2$) is a wide-bandgap oxide with attractive processing versatility and emerging p-type semiconducting behaviour, making it a promising material system for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications. However, TeO$_2$-derived thin films prepared by scalable manufacturing processes, such as vacuum sublimation, can contain residual metallic Te$^0$ species that introduce trap states, limit hole transport, and promote carrier recombination. Here, we demonstrate a selenium alloying strategy to control the defect chemistry of vacuum-sublimed TeO$_x$ films. TeO$_2$:Se powder mixtures (90:10~wt\%) were thermally evaporated and subsequently annealed in air at 225~$^\circ$C for up to 9~h, yielding amorphous TeO$_x$:Se films with an optical bandgap of 0.98~eV under optimised conditions. Structural, chemical, optical, and electrical analyses show that prolonged annealing promotes Se redistribution, suppresses residual Te$^0$ to approximately 0.4\%, reduces the film's surface roughness, and shifts the valence-band edge. To evaluate the potential of TeO$_x$:Se for photovoltaic applications, we fabricated thin-film solar cells with an ITO/ZnO/TeO$_x$:Se/MoO$_x$/Ag architecture. Devices based on an 80~nm TeO$_x$:Se active layer annealed for 9~h exhibit optimal performance, with broadband photocurrent generation from 300 to 1000~nm, yielding an open-circuit voltage of 0.50~V, a short-circuit current density of 8.50~mA~cm$^{-2}$, a fill factor of 0.44, and a maximum power conversion efficiency of approximately 1.87\%. These results establish selenium-alloyed TeO$_x$ as a viable oxide-derived absorber for thin-film photovoltaics and highlight chemical-state control as an effective route for improving photovoltaic performance.

infographic.key_insight: Selenium alloying and prolonged annealing suppress residual metallic tellurium in amorphous TeOx films, enabling thin-film solar cells with approximately 1.87% peak efficiency.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Chemical-state control offers a route to improve oxide-derived photovoltaic absorbers prepared by vacuum sublimation.
method: Thermally evaporate a 90:10 wt% TeO2:Se powder mixture.
Anneal films in air at 225 °C for up to 9 hours.
Fabricate and evaluate ITO/ZnO/TeOx:Se/MoOx/Ag solar cells.
infographic.evidence_signal: The optimal 80 nm absorber annealed for 9 hours achieved 0.50 V open-circuit voltage, 8.50 mA/cm² short-circuit current density, 0.44 fill factor, and approximately 1.87% efficiency, with photocurrent response from 300–1000 nm.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term device stability or manufacturing throughput for the 9-hour annealing process.

title: Explainable AI for Solar PV Power Forecasting: From Model Selection to Trustworthy, Reproducible Deployment
authors: Nuzhat Khan, Muhammad Paend Bakht, Ab Al-Hadi Ab Rahman, Fabiano Pallonetto, Amy Fahy, Mohamed Khalafalla Hassan
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is now a standard tool for forecasting the output of solar photovoltaic (PV) plants, yet published accuracy figures are often hard to compare and harder to trust. Many studies validate with random splits, report no reference forecast, and present feature attributions without saying what they can and cannot show. This paper reviews the main families of ML methods for PV power forecasting and resource assessment, from tree ensembles to deep and foundation models, and sets out a reproducible workflow that combines automated model search with explainable AI. The workflow is then tested on an openly available dataset: a 16.32 kWp plant in Porto, Portugal, forecast one day ahead from a 4 km numerical weather prediction grid. Over a full test year, the best models reach a normalised root mean square error (nRMSE) of 11.6% of installed capacity, about half the error of smart persistence. The choice of input features changed accuracy far more than the choice among strong algorithms, and shuffled cross-validation was mildly optimistic. After conformal calibration, the nominal 80% prediction intervals covered 81.7% of observations, against 64.5% before. SHAP rankings stayed stable when the model was retrained on different periods but shifted when correlated inputs were removed, so attributions should be read as properties of a model rather than of the plant. The paper closes with practical lessons and open problems, including deployment on edge hardware and the effect of a changing climate.

infographic.key_insight: For day-ahead solar PV forecasting, input feature selection mattered more than the choice among strong algorithms, with the best models achieving 11.6% nRMSE.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Reproducible evaluation, reference forecasts and calibrated prediction intervals can make PV forecasts more trustworthy for operational deployment.
method: Combine automated model search with explainable AI.
Evaluate day-ahead forecasts against smart persistence and examine validation-split effects.
Calibrate prediction intervals with conformal methods and test SHAP attribution stability.
infographic.evidence_signal: On an open dataset from a 16.32 kWp Porto plant using 4 km weather forecasts, a full test year showed roughly half the error of smart persistence and 81.7% coverage for calibrated nominal 80% intervals, versus 64.5% before calibration.

title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
authors: Nabanita Sarker, Hafiz Imtiaz
abstract: Machine learning coupled with device simulation is widely used to optimize thin-film solar cells, but almost exclusively in the forward direction, from device parameters to predicted performance. The inverse problem encountered after fabrication, namely identifying the mechanism that limits a given device, is still addressed by manual inspection of characterization data. In this work, both directions are examined for lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells using approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations. Replacing the Spiro-OMeTAD hole transport layer with CuI increases the simulated power conversion efficiency from 19.6\% to 21.6\%, almost entirely through the fill factor. Surrogate models trained and tested on a factorial parameter grid substantially overstate their predictive accuracy. An XGBoost regressor attains $R^2 = 0.9997$ on held-out grid points but only 0.58 on independently sampled devices, whereas training on a Latin hypercube design of comparable size restores $R^2 = 0.995$. For the inverse problem, a multi-label classifier identifies which of six degradation mechanisms are present from simulated temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit-voltage measurements. It achieves a macro $F_1$ score of 0.938, compared to 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline. The classifier does not, however, generalize to combinations of mechanisms absent from the training set.

infographic.key_insight: Machine learning can identify degradation mechanisms in simulated lead-free RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells, but its reliability depends on training coverage and sampling design.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could support post-fabrication diagnosis from electrical measurements, while replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through fill-factor improvement.
method: Generate approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D device simulations.
Compare forward-performance surrogates trained on factorial-grid and Latin-hypercube samples.
Use temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage to classify six potentially co-occurring degradation mechanisms.
infographic.evidence_signal: The diagnostic classifier achieves macro F₁ = 0.938 versus 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline; grid-trained XGBoost drops from R² = 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices, while Latin-hypercube training achieves 0.995.
infographic.watch_item: Results are simulation-based, and the diagnostic classifier does not generalize to mechanism combinations absent from training.
infographic.paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements

title: Properties of [111]-oriented ferroelectric superlattices based on oxides with a perovskite structure
authors: A. I. Lebedev
abstract: The ground-state structures of fifteen free-standing [111]-oriented ferroelectric superlattices (SLs) based on perovskite oxides and involving a single-atom substitution---BaTiO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$, PbTiO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$, PbTiO$_3$/PbZrO$_3$, SrZrO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$, PbZrO$_3$/BaZrO$_3$, BaTiO$_3$/BaZrO$_3$, PbTiO$_3$/BaTiO$_3$, BaTiO$_3$/CaTiO$_3$, KNbO$_3$/KTaO$_3$, KNbO$_3$/NaNbO$_3$, SrTiO$_3$/SrHfO$_3$, BaTiO$_3$/BaSnO$_3$, PbTiO$_3$/CaTiO$_3$, SrTiO$_3$/CaTiO$_3$, and PbZrO$_3$/SrZrO$_3$---are calculated from first principles. It is shown that in eleven considered SLs the ground state is ferroelectric. A distinctive feature of the structure of the superlattices is that both the ferroelectric distortions and the distortions associated with octahedral rotations are described by phonons at the $Γ$~point of the Brillouin zone. The importance of taking into account structural distortions associated with octahedral rotations, which in some cases lead to significant changes in the ferroelectric properties of SLs, is demonstrated. The thermodynamic stability of superlattices grown in the [111] and [100] directions is compared. An analysis of the force constants of the superlattices helps to explain the peculiarities of the ferroelectric properties of the superlattices and the corresponding solid solutions.

infographic.key_insight: First-principles calculations predict ferroelectric ground states in 11 of 15 [111]-oriented perovskite-oxide superlattices, with octahedral rotations sometimes substantially changing ferroelectric properties.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Accounting for octahedral rotations can guide the design of ferroelectric oxide heterostructures, although the abstract reports no AI methods or solar-cell performance.
method: Calculate ground-state structures of 15 free-standing superlattices from first principles.

infographic.watch_item: Predictions for free-standing structures require validation under practical substrate strain and growth conditions.

title: Should Belgians Install an Advanced Energy Management System in Their Electrified Dwelling ?
authors: Julian Ruddick, Cedric De Cauwer, Thierry Coosemans, Maarten Messagie
abstract: As dwellings electrify and more complex electricity pricing spreads in Belgium, the question arises: What are the potential benefits of installing an advanced energy management systems in an electrified Belgian dwelling ? To answer this question, we simulate 500 representative Belgian dwellings in which fossil systems are replaced by controllable electric technologies: space heating via air-to-air heat pumps, domestic hot water via electric boilers, and private transport via electric vehicles with home chargers. Photovoltaic systems are assigned according to current adoption rates. We evaluate two advanced energy management systems (EMS): model predictive control (MPC) and TreeC, a machine learning method using decision trees to model the EMS strategy. These are compared to a rule-based controller (RBC) that mimics default operation and an MPC with perfect forecasts (MPC P) as an upper bound. Performance for these EMSs is assessed for 2023 under a real contract with hourly prices and a monthly peak tariff. Average annual savings versus RBC are 82.5 EUR, 116.6 EUR, and 177.4 EUR for TreeC, MPC, and MPC P, respectively. All EMSs deliver similar thermal comfort (26-31 Kh). MPC saves more, while TreeC achieves higher EV charge completion (93.3% vs 88.8% for MPC, with a max charge of 95%) and a smoother aggregate load across the 500 dwellings. Savings remain modest relative to EMS purchase (280-680 EUR) and subscription (0-360 EUR/year) costs which is not favourable towards widespread adoption. The data and code to reproduce this study are available at https://github.com/EVERGi/should_belgians_install_advanced_ems_paper.

infographic.key_insight: Advanced energy management delivers modest savings in electrified Belgian homes: €82.5/year for TreeC and €116.6/year for MPC versus default-like control.
infographic.engineering_relevance: MPC offers greater bill savings, while decision-tree-based TreeC provides higher EV charge completion and smoother aggregate electricity demand.
method: Simulate 500 representative Belgian dwellings with heat pumps, electric boilers, EV chargers, and photovoltaics assigned at current adoption rates.
Compare TreeC and model predictive control against rule-based control and perfect-forecast MPC.
Evaluate 2023 operation under hourly electricity prices and a monthly peak tariff.
infographic.evidence_signal: Simulations show similar thermal comfort across controllers; TreeC achieves 93.3% EV charge completion versus 88.8% for MPC, against a 95% maximum.
infographic.watch_item: Annual savings may not justify reported EMS purchase costs of €280–680 and subscription fees of €0–360/year; results are simulation-based.
infographic.paper_title: Should Belgians Install an Advanced Energy Management System in Their Electrified Dwelling ?

title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
authors: Thanh Tung Huynh, Yuefeng Yin, Weiyao Zhao, Junlin Yan, Qurat Ul Ain, Jacek J. Jasieniak
abstract: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors. With hole doping the response recovers, and at densities reachable by electric double-layer gating CsPbI3 attains the spin Hall conductivity of p-GaAs. The response is therefore determined by the position of the halide-p bands relative to the valence band maximum, not by the atomic spin-orbit constant, a criterion that applies to any semiconductor with an orbital-singlet band edge. These results point to CsPbI3 as a candidate gate-controlled source of spin current for perovskite spin-orbit torque devices.

infographic.key_insight: Intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites is controlled by the energy position of halide-p bands relative to the valence-band maximum, rather than atomic spin–orbit strength.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Hole-gated CsPbI3 could provide a tunable spin-current source for perovskite spin–orbit torque devices, rather than a demonstrated solar-cell performance improvement.
method: First-principles calculations for CsPbBr3, CsPbI3, CsSnBr3 and CsSnI3.
Analysis of spin Berry curvature from spin–orbit-split halide-p bands.
Evaluation of intrinsic spin Hall conductivity versus Fermi level and hole density.
infographic.evidence_signal: Calculations locate the key halide-p bands 1.1–2.6 eV below the valence-band maximum and predict that CsPbI3 reaches p-GaAs-like spin Hall conductivity at hole densities accessible by electric double-layer gating.
infographic.watch_item: The results are computational predictions; experimentally achieving the required hole density while maintaining material stability and effective spin-current extraction remains to be demonstrated.
infographic.paper_title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites

title: Metadata-Driven AI: An Architectural Pattern for Sustainable Data Analysis with LLMs
authors: Renaud Pawlak, Armen Sulejmani, Jordi Cabot
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) let users analyse data in natural language, either by giving the data to the model to read directly or by having the model generate code to process it. Both routes send the data, or fragments of it, to the model; both pay for inference on every run; and the code a model writes to answer a question is usually discarded once the question is answered. We present Metadata-Driven AI, an architectural pattern that keeps the data away from the model and turns each analysis into a reusable program. Only metadata (not the actual data) crosses a one-way inference boundary to the LLM. The program the LLM returns runs next to the data and is kept, so that inference is paid once per analysis rather than once per run. We describe the pattern together with a simple cost model, a measurement of how little information crosses the boundary on public datasets, and a benchmark showing that a small, locally hosted model can serve as the generator. We illustrate the pattern on three applications, each built on a different implementation of it: geospatial photovoltaic prospection over live public APIs, extraction of portfolio positions from bank statements, and a conversational assistant over smart-city dashboards.

infographic.key_insight: Metadata-Driven AI keeps raw data away from the LLM and turns each generated analysis into a reusable program, reducing repeated inference.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For photovoltaic site prospection, this architecture supports analysis over live geospatial APIs while executing generated programs next to the data.
method: Send only metadata—not actual data—across a one-way inference boundary to the LLM.
Execute the generated analysis program next to the data.
Retain and reuse the program without new inference for each run.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports a cost model, metadata-transfer measurements on public datasets, a small locally hosted model benchmark, and three application demonstrations, including photovoltaic prospection.
infographic.watch_item: Generated programs still require validation, and changes to data schemas or APIs may require regeneration.
infographic.paper_title: Metadata-Driven AI: An Architectural Pattern for Sustainable Data Analysis with LLMs

title: Nonideal Absorbers in Hot-Carrier and Hot-Absorber Solar Cells: Losses and Heat Recycling
authors: Inés Durán, Simon A. Svatek, Irene Artacho, Elisa Antolín, Antonio Martí
abstract: The hot carrier solar cell exhibits a photovoltaic conversion efficiency limit of 85.4%. Among the idealizations necessary to achieve this efficiency, it has traditionally been considered essential that the electrons absorbing sunlight do not end up transferring the captured energy to the crystal lattice. In this work, we argue that such a requirement is not necessary if the absorber is thermally insulated. In our analysis, we also consider the possibility of ohmic losses in the absorber due to finite electrical conductivity. We also demonstrate that such losses, delivered as heat, can be partially recycled into electrical work with an efficiency that is given by the Carnot factor. The high efficiencies reported here are thermodynamic limits obtained with ideal energy-selective contacts and negligible parasitic contact conductance, not projections of practical device efficiency. Our work includes a sensitivity analysis for finite contact-mediated heat leakage, and the results are presented as design targets.

infographic.key_insight: Thermally insulating the absorber can relax the need to prevent electron-to-lattice energy transfer, while allowing some ohmic heat to be recycled into electrical work.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The analysis identifies thermal insulation, electrical conductivity, and suppression of contact heat leakage as design priorities for high-efficiency hot-carrier and hot-absorber solar cells.
method: Analyze thermally insulated absorbers with electron-to-lattice energy transfer.
Include ohmic losses from finite absorber conductivity and evaluate heat recycling.
Assess sensitivity to finite contact-mediated heat leakage.
infographic.evidence_signal: The thermodynamic analysis finds that ohmic heat can be partially recovered with an efficiency given by the Carnot factor and evaluates sensitivity to contact heat leakage.
infographic.watch_item: The cited 85.4% hot-carrier efficiency limit is not a practical device projection; high efficiencies require ideal energy-selective contacts and negligible parasitic contact conductance.
infographic.paper_title: Nonideal Absorbers in Hot-Carrier and Hot-Absorber Solar Cells: Losses and Heat Recycling

title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
authors: Mahmoud Samadpour, Alireza Fathi Beiraghvandi, Kazem Meraji, Tristan Sachsenweger Ballantyne, Fuxiang Ji, Mahdi Mohammadi
abstract: Surface morphology is widely considered an indicator of thin-film quality, with smoother films generally expected to exhibit more uniform optoelectronic properties. Here, we demonstrate that substantial surface evolution does not necessarily lead to increased electronic heterogeneity in mixed-dimensional perovskite heterostructures. We investigate how low-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper capping layers derived from the sterically hindered 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium cation affect the spatial distributions of photoluminescence (PL) characteristics and quasi-Fermi level splitting (QFLS) in 3D perovskites. By combining statistical atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis with confocal, spatially resolved PL spectroscopy, we correlate surface topography with microscale optoelectronic properties. Although capping increases surface roughness and height asymmetry, it does not increase electronic inhomogeneity. Instead, the heterostructures exhibit enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and improved spatial uniformity of radiative QFLS compared with pristine 3D films. Under accelerated aging, this contrast becomes more pronounced: pristine films develop substantial spatial fluctuations in emission and QFLS, whereas capped heterostructures largely preserve their optoelectronic homogeneity. These findings indicate that the low-dimensional capping layer suppresses aging-induced optoelectronic disorder, demonstrating that electronic uniformity can be maintained despite morphological irregularity. This decoupling provides a design principle for developing durable, high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving electronic uniformity, showing that morphology and optoelectronic quality can be decoupled.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a route to more durable perovskite photovoltaics without requiring smoother film surfaces.
method: Form Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium.
Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare pristine and capped films before and after accelerated aging.
infographic.evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, largely preserving optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports film-level evidence but provides no numerical device-efficiency gains or operational-lifetime results.
infographic.paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures

title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
authors: Mahesh Eledath-Changarath, Jesús Ortiga-Fibla, Andrés F. Gualdrón-Reyes, Jesús Rodríguez-Romero, Iván Mora-Seró, Ana Cros
abstract: Long-term stability remains a critical challenge limiting the photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites. In these materials, the choice of the organic spacer plays a key role not only in enhancing environmental stability, but also in determining their structural characteristics and carrier dynamics. Here, we present an environmental photo- and thermal-stability analysis of BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 two-dimensional lead halide perovskites by means of confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy techniques. We have investigated two different organic spacers, n-butylammonium (BA) and 2-phenylethylammonium (PEA), which provide comparable room-temperature luminescence in freshly exfoliated perovskite nanoflakes and degrade similarly through the removal of organic components and fast crystal phase decomposition into PbI2 and Pb0. However, we observed that the PEA organic cation significantly improves crystal morphology and suppresses lattice defects, resulting in slower degradation and enhanced resistance to light and thermal stress under ambient conditions. Our findings indicate that structural and chemical engineering, along with surface passivation and encapsulation strategies, are essential for achieving long-term stability in two-dimensional halide perovskite devices. Nevertheless, optimizing the balance between stability and device performance remains a critical consideration.

infographic.key_insight: PEA spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in 2D lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation under ambient light and thermal stress compared with BA spacers.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compare BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 with different organic spacers.
Probe environmental photo- and thermal-stability using confocal micro-Raman spectroscopy.
Analyze chemical degradation using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
infographic.evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated nanoflakes showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite sharing organic-loss and decomposition pathways to PbI2 and metallic Pb.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports material-level stability rather than solar-cell efficiency or device lifetime, so performance–stability trade-offs remain unresolved.
infographic.paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites

title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
authors: Ethan Berger, Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Lucas Svensson, Priyanka Deswal, Mehmet Baskurt
abstract: Perovskites have been studied for a wide range of applications, from oxide-based ferroelectrics to halide-perovskite photovoltaics. Despite their diverse functionalities, these materials share strong lattice anharmonicity arising from structural instabilities such as polar off-centering and octahedral tilting. These anharmonic distortions strongly influence the low-frequency vibrational response and can be observed in infrared (IR) and Raman spectra. However, low-frequency IR and Raman signatures are typically investigated separately, hindering the development of a unified understanding of vibrational spectroscopy across perovskite classes. In this work, we use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate the IR and Raman spectra of oxide perovskites (SrTiO$_3$ and BaTiO$_3$), halide perovskites (CsPbBr$_3$, CsSnBr$_3$, and CsGeBr$_3$) and double halide perovskites (Cs$_2$AgAlBr$_6$ and Cs$_2$AgBiBr$_6$). By comparing materials exhibiting polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities, we find that polar off-centering leads to enhanced low-frequency IR and dielectric responses, whereas nonpolar modes, particularly octahedral tilting, are associated with Raman central peaks. The strength of the low-frequency features also depends on how strongly the underlying modes couple to polarization or dielectric susceptibility. Finally, we show that the dynamics of these instabilities play an important role, with slow polar reorientations shifting the dielectric response to very low frequencies and overdamped tilting modes producing persistent Raman central peaks. These results establish a unified framework connecting low-frequency IR and Raman spectra to the symmetry, coupling and dynamics of their underlying anharmonic lattice instabilities.

infographic.key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
infographic.engineering_relevance: These spectral relationships could help researchers interpret lattice instabilities in perovskite photovoltaic materials, but do not directly demonstrate improved solar-cell performance.
method: Use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate infrared and Raman spectra.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites with polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities.
Relate spectral features to mode symmetry, coupling strength and lattice dynamics.
infographic.evidence_signal: Simulations across seven perovskites link slow polar reorientations to very-low-frequency dielectric responses and overdamped tilting modes to persistent Raman central peaks.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative accuracy metrics or experimental validation, leaving predictive reliability for device-relevant conditions uncertain.
infographic.paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites

title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
authors: Shiling Dong, Yongjie Wang, Hae-Jun Seok, Mengyuan Huang, Edward Newton, Der Ying Chen
abstract: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.5% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (44.2%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

infographic.key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers, supporting 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with perovskite sub-cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Improved carrier extraction in thicker AgBiS2 nanocrystal films offers a route toward stable, scalable near-infrared sub-cells for thin-film tandem photovoltaics.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange for one-step deposition of passivated, thicker nanocrystal films.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-light-absorbing perovskites in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months in dry air without encapsulation; triple-junction efficiencies exceeding 47.5% are modeled, not demonstrated.
infographic.watch_item: Realizing the modeled efficiency potential requires further transport improvements, while dry-air storage stability does not establish operational durability.
infographic.paper_title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics

title: Uncovering the Structural, Electronic, and Electrostatic Landscapes of SrTiO$_3$ Grain Boundaries via Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with a Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential
authors: Xing He, Kairi Masuda, Aaron M. Schankler, Songsong Zhou, Andrew M. Rappe
abstract: Grain boundaries in perovskites exhibit a rich variety of electronic, polar and magnetic properties, yet identifying their atomic structures and compositions remains challenging. Here, we combine the Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) method with a universal machine-learning interatomic potential to explore the coupled compositional and structural phase space of $Σ$5(310)[001] SrTiO$_3$ grain boundaries. The resulting chemical potential phase diagram identifies ten stable structures belonging to four motif families: large Sr kite, small Sr kite, incomplete Sr large kite, and Ti-rich structures. Extending the GCMC method to the Sigma5(210)[001] and Sigma17(410)[001] grain boundaries reveals how grain boundary plane and inclination angle influence the competition between small- and large-kite motifs. Density functional theory calculations of the predicted Sigma5(310)[001] grain boundaries show that the composition and atomic structure strongly govern the spatial distribution of conduction and valence band edge states, interfacial band alignment, and carrier localization. Four distinct electronic regimes emerge: localized electron-doped, delocalized electron-doped, insulating, and hole-attracting states. Our electrostatics analysis reveals the coexistence of the short-range electric fields at the reconstructed GB core associated with local atomic density and bonding, and the longer-range fields outside the core arising from the space charge. These fields can also couple to local polar distortions and generate composition-dependent polarization patterns. These results establish an efficient framework for exploring oxide perovskite grain boundary structures and reveal how stoichiometry and atomic reconstruction couple to electronic structure, electrostatics, and local polarization, providing a route toward predictive grain boundary engineering in functional perovskites.

infographic.key_insight: AI-assisted simulations reveal how SrTiO₃ grain-boundary composition and atomic structure control electronic states, electric fields, and local polarization.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The findings offer a route toward engineering oxide-perovskite interfaces, but do not directly demonstrate improved solar-cell performance.
method: Combine Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with a universal machine-learning interatomic potential.
Map stable grain-boundary structures across chemical potentials and boundary geometries.
Use density functional theory and electrostatic analysis to characterize electronic and polar behavior.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports ten stable Σ5(310)[001] structures in four motif families and four electronic regimes, with structural exploration extended to two other grain boundaries.
infographic.watch_item: Experimental validation and transferability to photovoltaic perovskites are not established in the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: Uncovering the Structural, Electronic, and Electrostatic Landscapes of SrTiO$_3$ Grain Boundaries via Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with a Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential
